newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU assembly clears TV programme rules.
newsitem.headline: EU assembly clears TV programme rules.

text.p: The European Parliament gave final approval on Tuesday to new European Union broadcasting legislation, which will leave Hollywood's domination of the bloc's television screens unchallenged.

The revised television without frontiers law, expected to cross its final hurdle when EU culture ministers meet in Luxembourg on June 30, will also guarantee European viewers can see major sporting events when exclusive rights are snapped up by pay television channels.

The process of revising the 1989 law, which lasted more than two years, became as complex as some of the soap operas that enthrall television viewers with France and the parliament fighting a vain rearguard action for stricter limits on the number of Hollywood films and sitcoms that can be shown.
"Sadly we missed a great opportunity to create a level playing field in the audiovisual sector," British Socialist Deputy Carole Tongue lamented in parliament.
"TV is Europe's Hollywood," she said dramatically. "It will help ensure that we create and view our own stories, be it Inspector Morse or Derrick."
The parliament did win rules forcing EU countries to respect each others' lists of major sporting events which must be shown free.
